title: SLO Governance and Customer Ops QBR Playbook
author: Asha Mehta
body:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines a repeatable SLO governance-centered QBR (Quarterly Business Review) and associated operational procedures for enterprise customers. It is intended to align Customer Success, SRE, and Account Engineering on what to measure, how to act on regressions, and the cadence for communication during onboarding and steady-state.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: enterprise accounts using Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments that require SLO-driven operational reviews.
- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), SREs, Account Engineers, Solutions Architects, and Customer stakeholders (technical leads).

High-level principles
---------------------
1. Make QBRs evidence-driven: every recommendation must reference metric trends or incident artifacts.
2. Tie remediation to economic impact (latency/cost/error-rate).
3. Default to short, repeatable actions: small policy changes + measurement cycles.
4. Use the same SLO definitions and dashboards across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to avoid measurement drift.

SLO catalog (recommended defaults)
--------------------------------
| SLO name | Target | Measurement window | Alert threshold | Owner | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| API p95 latency (generation) | < 350ms | 30d rolling | p95 > 450ms for 12h | eng-sre | User latency impacts product UX and token throughput |
| Request success rate (4xx/5xx) | >= 99.6% | 30d rolling | error rate < 99.0% for 6h | customer-success / eng-sre | Core availability for customer integrations |
| Token e2e cost per 1k tokens | <= baseline + 15% | 30d rolling | cost delta > +25% for 7d | customer-success/finance | Prevent billing shocks and ROI regressions |
| Embeddings recall on canonical dataset | >= 92% | 14d rolling | recall < 88% for 3d | applied-ml | Data quality regressions detected early |

Note: For Private deployments, measurement window may be locally configured — ensure telemetry export to centralized metrics when possible.

QBR cadence, agenda, and templates
----------------------------------
Cadence: Quarterly (standard), with accelerated QBRs triggered by:
- Repeated SLO breaches (three alerts in a 30d window)
- Post-migration or major model swap within 30 days
- Customer request following business-impacting event

Standard QBR agenda (60–90 minutes)
1) Welcome, participants, and outcomes (5 mins)
2) Health snapshot: SLOs and trend lines (10 mins)
3) Incident summary and root cause highlights since last QBR (10 mins)
4) Cost & utilization review (10 mins)
5) Model/feature changes and A/B results (10 mins)
6) Action items and owners (15 mins)
7) Open discussion / roadmap alignment (10–20 mins)

QBR slide checklist (deliverables to attach)
- Single-page SLO dashboard (p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput)
- Top 3 incidents with timelines and mitigations
- Cost-per-1000 token trend with annotation of config changes
- SLA/SLO compliance table for the quarter
- Action item register with owner+ETA

Operational playbook: SLO breach -> action path
------------------------------------------------
1. Detection and Triage (0–30 minutes)
   - Auto-alert on relevant channel (PagerDuty or shared Slack #customer-{id}-alerts).
   - Triage lead (SRE on-call) acknowledges within 15 minutes.
   - Quick snapshot: deployment hash, model name, route, region, recent deploys.

2. Short-term mitigation (30–240 minutes)
   - If latency spike: shift traffic to a lower-latency model variant or region (policy: canary fallback).
   - If error-rate spike: enable degraded-response mode (reduce max_tokens, disable streaming) or rollback last deploy.
   - Document mitigations in incident ticket and notify CSM.

3. Root Cause Analysis and Remediation (24–72 hours)
   - Post-incident RCA meeting within 72 hours.
   - Assign engineering/ML owners for code/runtime/model changes.
   - For cost regressions: run per-route costing job and propose batching/quantization changes.

4. QBR escalation and follow-up (quarterly/triggered)
   - If regression persists across measurement windows, schedule an accelerated QBR and include product leadership.

First-90-days operational checklist (onboarding)
------------------------------------------------
- Day 0–7: Account setup, API keys, basic integration test, confirm telemetry ingestion to customer dashboards.
- Day 7–30: Baseline SLO measurement; identify high-frequency routes and token distributions.
- Day 30–60: Apply initial performance optimizations (batching, KV cache hints, model variant routing).
- Day 60–90: Run a QBR-lite with customer stakeholders: show baseline, changes, and next 90-day plan.

Ownership matrix
----------------
| Activity | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Escalation contact |
| On-call triage | eng-sre | account-engineering | Pager duty SRE lead |
| SLO reporting | eng-platform | customer-success | Head of Analytics |
| Cost review | finance | customer-success | Billing ops |
| Model performance | applied-ml | account-engineering | Model onboarding lead |

Required dashboards and reports
------------------------------
- Live SLO dashboard (Grafana): p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, throughput per route/model/region.
- Cost report (daily): cost per route and per 1k tokens (CSV export).
- Embeddings quality (weekly): recall/precision on canonical prompt set.
- Onboarding audit (one-time): integration checklist with timestamps.

Example queries and snippets
---------------------------
Prometheus example (p95 latency over 30d):
- query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30d])) by (le, route))

SQL example (cost per route):
- SELECT route, SUM(cost_usd) / (SUM(tokens) / 1000) AS cost_per_1k_tokens
  FROM billing.events
  WHERE account_id = 'ACCOUNT_ID' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY route;

Slack/PD routing conventions
---------------------------
- Channel naming: #cust-{account_short}-alerts, #cust-{account_short}-ops (for runbook comms).
- PagerDuty: use service per product tier; escalate to on-call SRE for Sev>=2.

Customer comms templates
------------------------
- Immediate notification (post-detection)
  Subject: [Action required] {Account} SLO breach - {metric} - {short summary}
  Body: one-paragraph summary + link to incident ticket + expected ETA for mitigation.

- QBR invite template: include SLO snapshot and pre-read (2 slides). Request 30 minutes pre-brief with CSM + SRE.

Change policy for QBR recommendations
------------------------------------
- All QBR recommendations must include: technical owner, expected impact (metric delta), risk classification (low/medium/high), rollout plan, and rollback plan.
- Low-risk changes (config tweaks) can be executed by Account Engineering after CSM approval.
- Medium/high risk changes require a documented canary and SRE sign-off.

Post-QBR follow-up and tracking
-------------------------------
- Action items auto-created in Jira with labels: qbr/{account}/{quarter}. Owners update status weekly.
- CSM sends a 10-day check-in email summarizing progress on action items.
- Persistent items roll into the next QBR with additional monitoring.

Appendix: Example action register (CSV-friendly)
------------------------------------------------
- columns: action_id, account_id, short_description, owner, due_date, status, notes
- sample row: QBR-2024-07-001, ACCOUNT_123, "Reduce p95 by 40ms with KV cache hinting", account-eng-jane, 2024-08-10, in-progress, "Canary rolling now"

Appendix: Common recovery patterns and estimated times
------------------------------------------------------
- Traffic reroute to fall-back model variant: 5–20 minutes (automation + validation).
- Rollback to previous deployment: 10–30 minutes (depends on stateful caches).
- Apply batching/kv-cache tuning: 1–3 days (measure then iterate).
